key_insight: Hybrid quantum-classical PINNs had 38–44% fewer parameters but took at least 10× longer than the classical PINN at every measured stage.
engineering_relevance: Benchmark end-to-end derivative and training costs rather than using parameter count as a proxy for computational efficiency.
method: Tested a classical PINN, four hybrid configurations, and size-matched classical controls on 1D seawater temperature diffusion.
Timed four cumulative stages: forward pass, first and second input derivatives, and PDE-loss parameter gradients.
Varied qubit count, circuit depth, and batch size using CPU-simulated quantum circuits.
evidence_signal: Hybrids were 14–56× slower for forward passes and 10–97× slower for PDE-loss parameter gradients than the classical PINN, with approximately exponential runtime growth in qubit count over the tested range.
watch_item: These results concern CPU simulation on one benchmark; they do not establish runtime performance on physical quantum hardware.
paper_title: Fewer Parameters, Longer Runtimes: The Wall-Clock Cost of Hybrid Quantum Physics-Informed Neural Networks
